art_instructions: Inside the cozy classroom with soft blue walls and bright natural light, center the Owl at her same low honey‑oak desk by a large window; the desk fills the lower middle third of the frame and is angled slightly to the left. The Owl (chibi, 2–3 heads tall) sits on a small chair, green scarf visible, tiny satchel hanging from the chair back; her round amber eyes focus on the paper with a gentle smile and faint blush dots. One wing holds a thick red crayon touching a large white sheet on the desk, the other wing steadies the paper; show fresh red strokes to make the action of drawing unmistakable. On the paper, depict a simple picture: a square house with a triangle roof, a round yellow sun, and a green tree—only shapes and colors, no letters or numbers anywhere. Place a small cup of mixed crayons on the right side of the desk and a short brush and eraser to the left; a woven geometric rug sits under the desk for continuity with the classroom setting. In the background, include one or two empty low desks and a potted green plant near the window; keep everything simple and airy without any text or chalkboard writing. Use the Korean aegyo cute style with smooth monoline strokes, flat pastels, and minimal shading; let the red crayon and its fresh lines be the saturated accent. Compose at child eye level so the paper and Owl’s action are clearly visible, filling the frame with classroom elements while keeping silhouettes clean and readable.
